Changelog

Beta channel: 0.1.0-beta.x. Breaking changes ship in any beta release — each one is listed at the top of its entry below, with no migration scripts until 1.0. No silent breaks: removed verbs/flags fail loud naming the replacement.

Engine v2. Seven verbs, file-backed memory, MCP-only composition. For the version-matched agent contract at any time: agent-webmcp skill show.

Unreleased (beta)

Breaking: the config system is removed. No files, no schema, no served /config.json, no config key in doctor. The two launch options stay plain flags: --consequential allow|ask|deny (default ask, bad values exit 2) and --registry DIR. doctor reports policy: {value, source: flag|default}.

Breaking: the config file system is dead. Deleted: AGENT_WEBMCP_CONFIG, AGENT_WEBMCP_CONFIG_CONTENT, project/global files, walk-up, substitution. Policy is one flag per invocation: --consequential allow|ask|deny (default ask), garbage fails loud at startup. Enforcement must live server-side — the gated agent supplies confirm itself and project files can't constrain a harness-controlled cwd. Gate logic untouched; doctor reports flag or default.

Breaking: config shrinks to one key and the endpoint leaves it entirely. Deleted: browser.cdp (the driver feeds the endpoint per open call via cdp; discovery covers daemon → 9222/9229, else fail loud) and index.enabled (consult always, degrade on miss — the flag bought nothing). Remaining: permissions.conse- quential (ask|allow|deny, default ask), the safety catch on mutating page tools, opencode-shaped (same three effects; headless, so ask means the call must carry confirm: true). Old keys are ignored, not errors — no migration needed. Malformed files now warn

  • skip (opencode parseInfo) instead of failing loud on explicit paths; new {file:path} substitution for secrets.

Breaking: registry env deleted, global-main confirmed. AGENT_WEBMCP_REGISTRY is gone — mcp serve --registry DIR pins the root, otherwise project .agent-webmcp/registry/ overlays the user-global main store (reads merge, project wins). The double-append walk-up bug is fixed (production walk-up never hit; everything silently fell back to global). Malformed config files now warn + continue like opencode instead of failing loud on explicit paths; new {file:path} substitution for secrets (relative to the config file's dir).

Breaking: the engine no longer launches or owns a browser. open needs a reachable one (flag --cdp → browser.cdp → answering agent-browser daemon, else loopback 9222/9229, else fail loud naming the fix). --headed is rejected (display belongs to your browser); browser.{engine,headed,idleTimeout,profile} config keys are gone (unknown keys ignored, old files still parse); open output drops headed/borrowed; close closes its tab, never a browser. Install agent-browser (plus its Chrome) for the zero-setup path.

  • Config file (~/.config/agent-webmcp/config.json, project .agent-webmcp/config.json): browser.cdp (default endpoint; {env:} for tokens), index.enabled, permissions.consequential (ask|allow|deny, default ask; consequential verbs need execute {confirm: true}).
  • find verb: indexed-site search splits out of search (live verbs only again); open keeps its advisory index record; both honor index.enabled.
  • upgrade command: source upgrade in place (pull → gate → compile → reinstall with .prev backup). Refuses dirty trees and bare-bun runs.
  • Beta markers: version 0.1.0-beta.x, hero badge, doctor reports release: "beta".

0.1.0

  • Seven verbs: open list search register execute close unregister. Composition (search, execute) is MCP-only; the CLI mirrors lifecycle plus doctor, mcp list/serve, skill show.
  • Sessions: owned headless Chromium by default, --headed opt-in, --cdp borrows a foreign tab (it gets navigated — stated cost). close kills only owned browsers (TERM→wait→KILL, profile removed every path); foreign pids are never signaled.
  • Custom tools: spec plus plain-JS body, compiled debugger-side (CSP-exempt), fixture-proved before persisting (consequential tools hand-proved). Saved as <root>/<origin-slug>/<name>/{spec.json,body.js}; every open re-applies; rot surfaces as staleSuspect; recovery is re-register.
  • Codemode: search ranks across sessions with deterministic field weights; execute runs one program over flat or namespaced (sessions[]) tools with enforced budgets. Every envelope carries untrusted: true.
  • Honesty rules: piped output is JSON, writes need --yes, exits 0 ok / 2 usage / 1 failure with the message on stderr.
  • Install: Bun toolchain, Chromium 152+, source build (bun run gate, bun run compile); per-OS release binaries attach from this version on.

How to read this log

Entries name the verb or door they change and the evidence to expect (reapplied[], skipped[], staleSuspect, envelope fields). Behaviour strings quoted here match CLI and MCP output verbatim — if output and log ever disagree, the output wins and the log gets a correction entry.
